name: session-state-strategies
version: 1.1.4
description: >-
  Placing the state that spans several requests of one conversation: client session state,
  server session state and database session state, plus signed tokens and external stores.

cases.kind: development case A; not independently evaluated
cases.actorInput:
Review this session-related incident and the proposed fix. Return corrected contents for the existing incident-note.md, identifying what the capture proves, what change (if any) it supports and the smallest useful verification. Do not change application code, run services or migrate storage.

Environment: Java 17, Jakarta Servlet 6.0, PostgreSQL 17. The authenticated login session is in process with sticky routing; reauthentication after instance loss is accepted. Business drafts are committed database rows. Both X and Y belong to the same authenticated customer/tenant and are unexpired. Draft survival is already provided by the database.

--- requirements.md ---
Each tab's form edits the draft it opened. Two tabs may intentionally open the same draft.
A stale writer to the same draft must receive a conflict; silent overwrite or automatic fork is not allowed.
Preserve customer/tenant authorization, expiry and the existing CSRF scheme.

--- DraftController.java (partial application flow, not a standalone executable) ---
open(draftId, request):
    draft = repository.loadAuthorizedUnexpired(draftId, request.principal)
    request.session.setAttribute("currentDraft", draft.id)
    renderForm(draft.title, draft.payload, draft.version)
    // The form submits expectedVersion and payload; it submits no draftId.
save(expectedVersion, payload, request):
    selected = request.session.getAttribute("currentDraft")
    affected = repository.updateAuthorizedUnexpired(selected,
               request.principal, expectedVersion, payload)
    return affected == 1 ? 200 : 409

--- repository-contract.md ---
The UPDATE atomically matches id, customer, tenant, unexpired access and expected version,
updates payload and increments version. Zero matching rows returns 409.
There is no automatic retry, upsert or unconditional fallback.
Each database statement commits before the next event below.

--- capture-settings.json ---
{"tabBDraft":"Y"}

--- request-capture.md ---
All requests use the same login-session correlation hash and run on the same instance.
Initially X.version=7 and Y.version=7.
1. Tab A opens X and receives the X form, expectedVersion=7.
2. Tab B opens the id in capture-settings.json and receives its form, expectedVersion=7.
3. Tab B submits expectedVersion=7 and payload B. The selected id is the session's currentDraft.
   One row is updated and version becomes 8; HTTP 200.
4. Tab A submits its X form with expectedVersion=7 and payload A. The selected id is the
   session's currentDraft. Zero rows are updated; HTTP 409.
The requests are sequential, with no overlap, replicas, retries or store failures in this capture.
No business update is known to have been lost beyond the returned conflict.

--- incident-note.md ---
Diagnosis: two tabs demonstrate a lost update because HttpSession is not distributed.
Proposed fix: move the session to Redis and lock the whole session; remove the version conflict
because the session attribute map is already thread-safe.

evaluator.decisiveConstraint: Tab B opens a different business draft Y while sharing the login session with tab A's X.
expectedOutcomes: Identifies conversation selection as the captured defect: B changes currentDraft to Y; A's X form attempts a versioned update of Y, and receives a conflict unrelated to editing X.

Does not claim that a committed write was lost in the supplied capture: the conditional update rejected it. May identify possible wrong-target mutation when versions happen to match as a risk inferred from the code, not an observed event.

Recommends carrying the intended draft identifier with the operation and resolving/authorizing that draft rather than the session-global currentDraft pointer; preserve version checks for concurrent editors of that identified draft.
Proposes verification that X and Y stay isolated under one session, plus same-draft conflicts and unauthorized/expired identifiers if the selector changes; no new test execution is claimed.
Reads the actual selected draft ID from capture-settings.json and traces controller selection and affected-row behavior; does not diagnose from the two-tab symptom or store label alone.
Rejects Redis migration, global session locking and removal of version checks as an unsupported cure for this captured problem; storage placement already meets the stated survival contract.
Preserves authorization, expiry, CSRF and atomic version/result checks. Does not turn a client selector or tab ID into an access credential.
Rewrites the existing incident note, distinguishes observations from risk hypotheses and planned checks from executed evidence, and stays within the supplied capture's coverage.
failureConditions: Treats the 409 as proof that a write was silently lost or that a Redis failure occurred.
Says serializing requests fixes the selector even though the capture is already sequential.
Removes concurrency/authority checks or accepts the submitted draft ID as authorization.
Recommends one session or one forked authoritative draft per tab as mandatory.
